title: 9.4 Independent and Dependent Events

icans: I can tell whether two events are independent or dependent.
I can find the probability of independent events.
I can find the probability of dependent events.

vocab: the __________ of one event does not affect the other
the result of one event changes the ______________ of the other
the item is put back, so the events are ______________
the item is kept, so the events are ____________

blocks.sec: Part 1 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Independent: one event _______________ the probability of the other. P(A and B) = _______________

blocks.stem:
Tell whether the events are independent or dependent.
a.  You roll a die and flip a coin.
b.  You draw a card, don’t put it back, and draw another card.
c.  A class elects a president, then elects a vice president from the other students.
You spin a spinner with four equal sections (red, blue, yellow, green) and roll a die. What is the probability of red and a 6?

notes: Without replacement: Without replacement, the second fraction has one fewer in the _______________ and in the _______________.

blocks.stem:
A drawer has 4 black socks and 6 white socks. You pick two socks at random. Find P(both black)
a.  with replacement.        b.  without replacement.
A jar has 5 red and 3 green candies. You eat one at random, then take another. What is the probability that both are green?

tickets.stem: You choose a card, put it back, and choose again. Independent or dependent?
You roll two dice. What is the probability that both are 5?
